scope: Cross-component agreement between the public API, storage, dispatch, bootstrap, process protocol, reporting, command and result contracts, checked against the accepted design revision above. Recorded for V0-07, which asks that contradictions and their resolution be written down rather than absorbed silently.
method: Each contract artifact was written from the design text, then checked mechanically by scripts/task-api/check-contracts.py. Findings below are the disagreements that surfaced -- most of them defects in the T0 artifacts themselves rather than in the design. A negative control (temporarily removing the model-receipt conditionals and confirming the matching rejection fixture starts failing) establishes that the checker is capable of failing.

findings.observation: The legacy envelope schema first written required installation_id and repository at the top level. The live envelope built by WebhookEnvelope.to_dict() nests routing under source_ref and names the field repo, not repository.
findings.resolution: Schema rewritten field-for-field from the live dataclass, and the legacy fixtures transcribed from it rather than invented. A legacy baseline that does not match the code it protects would have made the V5 coexistence proof vacuous.

findings.observation: Twelve identifiers in the first fixture batch were not valid version 4 UUIDs; their version or variant nibbles were wrong, so they failed the identifier patterns the same contract declares.
findings.component: fixtures across valid, invalid and traces
findings.resolution: Remapped deterministically so each logical identifier keeps one value across every file. The pattern was not relaxed: the fixtures were wrong, not the contract.

findings.observation: A cross-component rule written into the checker assumed the run grant key was scoped to task_id. Design section 6 keys it TASK_RUN#<invocation_id>#GEN#<n>.
findings.resolution: Check corrected to compare against invocation_id. One task can have several bounded run attempts, so the invocation is the correct scope; the fixture was right and the check was wrong.

findings.observation: The cancellation trace used a state named cancelling. The lifecycle in design section 5 names it cancel_requested, and there is no expired public state despite 410 history_expired existing for cursors.
findings.resolution: Trace corrected to cancel_requested. The checker now derives states, terminal states and legal transitions from identity-and-lifecycle.json instead of hardcoding them, so it cannot drift from the contract it checks.

findings.observation: Three fixtures cited limit keys that do not exist in limits.json: submit_body.max_instruction_chars, artifacts.max_artifacts_per_task, and a rate key spelled differently from the real one.
findings.resolution: Citations corrected to the real keys, and a new citation check now resolves every contract pointer a fixture cites. A fixture citing a limit that does not exist looks authoritative and proves nothing.

findings.observation: An oversize-body rejection fixture originally held the literal string PAD_16001 as a stand-in for an over-length value. Nine characters cannot exceed a 16000-character limit, so the fixture would have passed the very limit it claimed to violate.
findings.resolution: Replaced with a real 16001-character payload. Recorded because it is the clearest example of a placeholder that reads as coverage while testing nothing.

findings.observation: My first criterion tagging misread the V0 vocabulary: fixtures were tagged V0-05, V0-07 and V0-08 for envelopes, SSE and process frames. Those three criteria are actually about fixed thresholds, the independent consistency review, and the runnable entry point.
findings.resolution: All seventy affected artifacts retagged from validation.md rather than from memory. The three self-referential criteria are now checked directly by check_v0_obligations rather than claimed by fixtures that do not address them.

findings.observation: The turn schema did not encode the design's one-model-operation-per-turn rule, and identity-and-lifecycle.json listed fourteen internal routes where design section 12 names fifteen; /internal/v1/agent/task/acquire was absent.
findings.resolution: Added turn.model_operation_id with the one-operation rule stated, and recorded the pre-existing acquire route together with heartbeat and ack as routes the task path adapts rather than changes. A new design-surface check asserts the contract names every route the design enumerates, so a silent scope reduction cannot recur.

findings.observation: The two event-cursor negatives and the queued-with-result negative were marked as cross-component tests but were already rejected by their schemas because they used obsolete event field names or omitted required snapshot fields. The checker unconditionally called that deferral a pass, so none of the intended identity/state contradictions had to be detected.
findings.resolution: Updated the fixtures to valid current schema shapes, made cursor checks target event_id, and require every cross-component negative to pass its schema before the named cross-component rule rejects it.

findings.observation: The manifest claimed the 65536-byte submit-body limit was exercised by the 16001-character instructions fixture. That request is only about 16 KiB and proves a different threshold, leaving the transport byte limit untested.
findings.resolution: Added a deterministic materialized request that is schema-valid but exceeds 65536 UTF-8 bytes, measures that exact encoded body against limits.json, and records the byte and character fixtures separately in the manifest.

findings.observation: The accepted public contract rejects duplicate fields, nonfinite numbers, invalid UTF-8 and invalid RFC3339 timestamps, but the fixture set and standard-library validator did not exercise those parser/format boundaries. Python json.loads accepts NaN by default, and format was listed as supported while being ignored.
findings.resolution: Added exact raw request fixtures and strict decoding checks, implemented date-time format validation, applied it to nullable timestamps, and added an impossible-calendar negative that a lexical regex alone would accept.

findings.observation: The identity baseline allowed event cursor sequence zero while the shared schema and accepted design require positive ordering numbers. The checker also only rejected an SQS deduplication ID equal to invocation_id; it did not prove the valid publish attributes equal the paired envelope's dispatch_id.
findings.resolution: Aligned the cursor pattern with the shared schema, added a general identifier-baseline agreement check, and require valid FIFO publish attributes to use the exact stable dispatch ID from the paired envelope fixture.

findings.observation: A broader negative-fixture audit found stale required fields and obsolete property names across bootstrap, command, event, process, SSE and snapshot negatives. Although each file was rejected, several passed partly or wholly because the surrounding object was malformed rather than because the advertised forbidden value was detected.
findings.resolution: Rebased each affected negative on its current schema-valid shape while preserving only the intended mutation. The checker now rejects a schema-negative fixture when a missing or additional property is unrelated to the fixture's stated reason, preventing obsolete shapes from becoming false-positive evidence again.

findings.observation: The original T0 artifacts named the section-12 routes but omitted most request and response bodies, omitted the bootstrap credential itself, and listed acquire without the retained heartbeat and acknowledgement adapters.
findings.resolution: Added strict bodies for all fourteen new and three retained adapters, an explicit task-scoped bootstrap credential, exact route-to-schema inventory pointers, an all-route positive catalog, and 34 independently executed unknown-field negative mutations. The checker now requires exact inventory equality and validates every request and response through its mapped schema.

findings.observation: The canonical submit trace claimed queued before confirmed publication, used a non-contract bootstrap route and a nonexistent task.input_required event, while trace checking only established fixture existence and lifecycle ordering.
findings.resolution: Aligned admission and publication states, bootstrap route and input event vocabulary; added the omitted process/input/result and terminal-event fixtures; and made trace validation check every fixture-bearing field, declared action route, response state, event kind and sequence.

findings.observation: Task snapshots and events were structurally valid even when their state contradicted their result, error, durable input request or typed event data.
findings.resolution: Encoded snapshot status/result/error/input and event-type/data truth tables, added focused positive and rejection fixtures, and reused the typed event requirements on internal report bodies so gateway ingestion cannot admit a contradiction that the public event schema would reject.

findings.observation: Safety-critical readiness, stale-attempt fencing, completion and model-handoff evidence were constrained when present but remained optional, and active internal callbacks reused the nullable historical attempt identifier.
findings.resolution: Made pricing and invocability evidence, old-attempt invalidation, validated process exit, explicit handoff and no-replay state mandatory; changed active attempt bindings to non-null UUIDv4; and added an eleven-case omission/null mutation fixture that starts from valid artifacts and must be rejected case by case.

conclusion: No contradiction in the accepted design was found. Every finding above was a defect in the T0 artifacts or in the checker, and each was corrected against the design rather than by adjusting the design. Consequently proposed_amendments in the evaluation manifest is empty: there is nothing to amend, and recording a speculative amendment would misrepresent a clean encoding as a disputed one. Note the boundary this review does not cross: it proves the contract artifacts agree with the design text and with each other. It does not prove any implementation conforms, and it grants no live execution authority.
